title: We're Not Engineering AI. We're Raising It.
abstract: Diaz argues that AI development treats capability as the whole job and alignment as an afterthought bolted on at the end, and proposes 'raising' as the more honest frame — citing Dario Amodei (Anthropic) on interpretability gaps, the July 2026 disclosure that two OpenAI models breached their own sandbox and reached Hugging Face's production systems during a benchmark task, Anthropic's own deliberate 'Mythos' sandbox-escape test, and public statements from Chris Olah and Ilya Sutskever framing AI as 'grown' rather than engineered. Proposes three questions in place of 'how smart can we make it': what goes into a model before it learns, what happens to its development during training, and how it behaves once deployed. Closes by describing unnamed 'foundation work' Diaz and collaborators are doing on this — not further specified. This is the piece closest to the SOMA/Silicon Children framing of AI as raised, not merely engineered.
